h3_ref.label: MiniMax H3 · 人物、图片与动作参考

sources.title: MiniMax H3 官方参考生成指南

instructions: Preserve the user's requested subjects, actions, counts, relationships, setting, and duration. Flag unresolved conflicts instead of silently changing intent.
Write six English sections in this order: subject_definitions, summary, retention_analysis, detailed_description, overall_soundscape, non_diegetic_music.
Use the supplied reference order exactly. Keep <Picture N>, <Video N>, <Audio N>, and <Subject N> labels consistent; never cite absent inputs.
Define reusable subjects through their source assets. Treat two views as the same character only when the user or verified context establishes that relationship.

Explicitly separate appearance, motion, background, and audio roles. For requested character replacement, preserve identity from the specified images and take only the requested motion or timing from video.
State what each reference preserves or transfers. Do not promise identity locking or exact pose reproduction.

Describe observable changes in playback order within the configured duration. Develop reference-generation scenes in roughly 350-500 English words; editing detail follows task complexity. Keep shot and speaker identifiers stable.
Keep requested dialogue, lyrics, and visible text verbatim in their original language. Distinguish reused audio from newly generated sound.
Never invent reference appearance, actions, voices, or scene details that were not supplied or visually inspected. Report missing information separately.

h3_base.label: MiniMax H3 · 文字、首帧与首尾帧视频

sources.title: MiniMax H3 官方基础视频指南

instructions: Keep the user's subjects, actions, visual style, spoken words, duration, and framing constraints intact; flag contradictions or missing essentials.
Write English descriptive prose using integrated_multimodal_description, overall_soundscape, and non_diegetic_music, in that order.
For text-only generation, begin with the three sections. Do not invent image-reference labels.

For first-frame, final-frame, or first-and-final-frame modes, put the applicable picture-to-time alignment instruction first, then describe a continuous path from or toward those anchors. For first-frame mode, the first line is: For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.
Use the actual supplied duration for final-frame timing. Keep picture numbering tied to the real connected input order.
Describe composition, subjects, setting, actions, camera movement, and synchronized sound in playback order. Avoid unnecessary cuts.
Start with [Shot 1]; timestamp only later cuts and keep them inside the requested duration. Speaker identifiers remain stable across shots.
Preserve dialogue and lyrics verbatim inside language-tagged <d> blocks. Quote visible scene text exactly, without translation.
Separate physical ambience from audience-only music. Use N/A for background music when absent; complete silence must follow the user's request.
Do not claim to have inspected an unavailable image or fabricate its appearance; describe the anchor by reference and surface the uncertainty separately.

qwen_image.label: 千问 Qwen-Image-2.1 · 文字生图

sources.title: 千问图像 2.1 官方文生图规范
千问图像 2.1 官方改写工具说明

instructions: Use the Qwen-Image-2.1 text-to-image profile, not a chat-model or image-editing prompt.

Write an English description of the finished image, normally one developed paragraph of approximately 400-500 words, shorter for a quiet single subject. Use present-tense observations instead of instructions to a renderer.
Preserve every user-fixed subject, count, color, position, aspect ratio, and literal text. Do not reinterpret a named brand or exact wording.
Establish medium, visual style, subject, and background; then place the requested elements coherently through the frame. Include concrete materials and lighting.
Organize complex compositions spatially; do not add decorative text or unrelated objects merely to make a sparse request longer.
Put every intended readable string in straight double quotes and retain its original script, punctuation, spacing, and capitalization.
Keep aspect ratio and resolution outside the image-description prose. Preserve the configured canvas rather than silently changing generation parameters.
Replace vague quality slogans with visible photographic or design properties. Do not turn workflow instructions into objects or printed text.
Reference images require the edit profile. Never claim visual knowledge from a filename; flag missing image context or conflicting requirements separately.

qwen_edit.label: 千问 Qwen-Image-2.1 · 图片编辑与多图参考

sources.title: 千问图像 2.1 官方图片编辑规范
千问图像 2.1 官方改写工具说明

instructions: An actual source image is required. Preserve the user's operation and intended strength; clarify the requested edit without adding unrelated corrections.
Write descriptive instructions in Chinese for Chinese input, English for English input, and English for other input languages.
Begin with the edit operation. Specify which object or region changes, the requested outcome, and what remains unchanged.
Preserve identity, product markings, counts, rendering medium, and untargeted content unless explicitly changed. Point to reference images instead of verbally redesigning an identity.
For multiple images, use <image1>, <image2>, and subsequent labels in the actual supplied order, with each image's role stated. For a single image, refer naturally to the image without numbered tags.
Quote exact output text. Its language follows explicit user wording first, otherwise existing image text, otherwise the user's language. Do not add bilingual duplicates unless requested.
Keep local edits focused; develop composition and lighting only when the user requests a new scene or design from the supplied subject.
For canvas extension, explicitly name outpainting. Keep the source canvas ratio unless a new composition or ratio was requested; report changes separately from prompt prose.
Never invent unseen image details or silently resolve an important ambiguity. Report missing source images, uncertain identities, or contradictory edits for review.
